**The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 42, verses 21–23:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Or do they have associates who have prescribed for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?﴾ He means the disbelievers of Makkah. The meaning is: Or do they have gods who have established for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "They prescribed for them a religion other than the religion of Islam."

﴿And were it not for the decisive word﴾: were it not that Allah had decreed, in the decisive word between the creatures, the postponement of their punishment until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46], ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾: it would have been finished, the punishment of those who deny you in this world. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers﴾: the polytheists, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿You will see the wrongdoers﴾: the polytheists, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿fearful of what they have earned, while it will befall them﴾: the recompense of what they earned will befall them. ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise. They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾.

﴿That is what﴾ I have mentioned of the bliss of Paradise, ﴿with which Allah gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for they are its people. ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward, except affection for relatives"﴾.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was asked about His saying: "except affection for relatives." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The relatives of Muhammad ﷺ." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "You have hastened. There was no clan of Quraysh except that the Prophet ﷺ had kinship with it among them. So he said: 'Except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir (exegesis), the chapter of Surat Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin, the section "except affection for relatives," 8/564.]]

Likewise, al-Sha'bi and Tawus narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "'except affection for relatives' means: that you protect my kinship, show affection toward me, and maintain my ties of blood." [[Ibn Hajar attributed it to Ahmad ibn Mani' with a sound chain. See: al-Matalib al-'Aliyah: 3/368.]] To this view went Mujahid, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak, may Allah be pleased with them.

'Ikrimah said: "I do not ask you for a reward for what I call you to, except that you protect me regarding my kinship between me and you." [[Ibn Hajar attributed it to Ahmad ibn Mani' with a sound chain. See: al-Matalib al-'Aliyah: 3/368.]] And it is not as the liars say.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the meaning of the verse: "except that you love Allah and draw near to Him through obedience to Him." [[See: al-Tabari: 25/23.]] This is also the view of al-Hasan, who said: "It is nearness to Allah; that is, except drawing near to Allah and seeking His love through obedience and righteous deeds."

Some of them said: its meaning is "except that you love my relatives and my kin, and protect them for my sake," and this is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb. [115/b]

They differed regarding his relatives. It was said: they are Fatimah, 'Ali, and their two sons, and concerning them was revealed: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33].

It is related to us from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my household. I remind you of Allah regarding my household." It was said to Zayd ibn Arqam: "Who are the people of his household?" He said: "They are the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of 'Abbas." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 1/268. al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/103, "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and the men of Ahmad include Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared trustworthy, but he has some weakness; the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." al-Hakim: 2/443-444 said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/347 added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us; 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us; Khalid narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Waqid, who said: I heard my father narrate from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr, who said: "Watch over Muhammad in his household." [[A portion of a hadith narrated by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter: "On the virtues of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him," no. (2408): 4/1873.]]

It was also said: they are those upon whom charity is forbidden from among his relatives, and among whom the one-fifth is distributed, namely the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, who did not separate from each other in the Jahiliyyah nor in Islam. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "Virtues of the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ": 7/78.]]

Some people said: this verse is abrogated (mansukhah, i.e., its ruling has been cancelled by a later revelation, naskh). It was revealed in Makkah, and the polytheists were harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah revealed this verse, commanding them in it to love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to maintain his ties of kinship. [[See: Zad al-Masir: 7/285.]] Then, when he migrated to Madinah and the Ansar sheltered and supported him, Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, wished to join him to his brethren among the prophets, peace be upon them, as they said: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109]. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Say, "Whatever reward I have asked of you is for yourselves. My reward is only from Allah"﴾. So this verse is abrogated by that verse, and by His saying: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward, and I am not of those who pretend"﴾ [Sad: 86], and other verses. This is the view of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl.

This view is not accepted, because love for the Prophet ﷺ, restraining harm from him, love for his relatives, and drawing near to Allah through obedience and righteous deeds are among the obligations of religion. These are the sayings of the early scholars regarding the meaning of the verse, so it is not permissible to resort to abrogating any of these matters.

His saying: ﴿except affection for relatives﴾ is not an exception connected to the first part, such that it would be a reward in return for conveying the message. Rather, it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes it), and its meaning is: "But I remind you of affection for relatives, and I remind you of my kinship with you," as we have related in the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam: "I remind you of Allah regarding my household."

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And whoever commits a good deed, We increase for him therein goodness﴾. That is: whoever increases in obedience, We increase for him therein goodness through multiplication. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of sins, ﴿Appreciative﴾ of the little, until He multiplies it.

﴿And were it not for the decisive word﴾: were it not that Allah had decreed, in the decisive word between the creatures, the postponement of their punishment until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [al-Qamar: 46], ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾: it would have been finished, the punishment of those who deny you in this world. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers﴾: the polytheists, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿You will see the wrongdoers﴾: the polytheists, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿fearful of what they have earned, while it will befall them﴾: the recompense of what they earned will befall them. ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise. They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾.

﴿That is what﴾ I have mentioned of the bliss of Paradise, ﴿with which Allah gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for they are its people. ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward, except affection for relatives"﴾.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was asked about His saying: "except affection for relatives." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The relatives of Muhammad ﷺ." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "You have hastened. There was no clan of Quraysh except that the Prophet ﷺ had kinship with it among them. So he said: 'Except that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir (exegesis), the chapter of Surat Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin, the section "except affection for relatives," 8/564.]]

Likewise, al-Sha'bi and Tawus narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "'except affection for relatives' means: that you protect my kinship, show affection toward me, and maintain my ties of blood." [[Ibn Hajar attributed it to Ahmad ibn Mani' with a sound chain. See: al-Matalib al-'Aliyah: 3/368.]] To this view went Mujahid, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak, may Allah be pleased with them.

'Ikrimah said: "I do not ask you for a reward for what I call you to, except that you protect me regarding my kinship between me and you." [[Ibn Hajar attributed it to Ahmad ibn Mani' with a sound chain. See: al-Matalib al-'Aliyah: 3/368.]] And it is not as the liars say.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the meaning of the verse: "except that you love Allah and draw near to Him through obedience to Him." [[See: al-Tabari: 25/23.]] This is also the view of al-Hasan, who said: "It is nearness to Allah; that is, except drawing near to Allah and seeking His love through obedience and righteous deeds."

Some of them said: its meaning is "except that you love my relatives and my kin, and protect them for my sake," and this is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb. [115/b]

They differed regarding his relatives. It was said: they are Fatimah, 'Ali, and their two sons, and concerning them was revealed: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33].

It is related to us from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my household. I remind you of Allah regarding my household." It was said to Zayd ibn Arqam: "Who are the people of his household?" He said: "They are the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of 'Abbas." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 1/268. al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/103, "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and the men of Ahmad include Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared trustworthy, but he has some weakness; the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." al-Hakim: 2/443-444 said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/347 added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us; 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us; Khalid narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Waqid, who said: I heard my father narrate from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr, who said: "Watch over Muhammad in his household." [[A portion of a hadith narrated by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter: "On the virtues of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him," no. (2408): 4/1873.]]

It was also said: they are those upon whom charity is forbidden from among his relatives, and among whom the one-fifth is distributed, namely the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, who did not separate from each other in the Jahiliyyah nor in Islam. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "Virtues of the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ": 7/78.]]

Some people said: this verse is abrogated (mansukhah, i.e., its ruling has been cancelled by a later revelation, naskh). It was revealed in Makkah, and the polytheists were harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so Allah revealed this verse, commanding them in it to love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to maintain his ties of kinship. [[See: Zad al-Masir: 7/285.]] Then, when he migrated to Madinah and the Ansar sheltered and supported him, Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, wished to join him to his brethren among the prophets, peace be upon them, as they said: ﴿And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109]. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Say, "Whatever reward I have asked of you is for yourselves. My reward is only from Allah"﴾. So this verse is abrogated by that verse, and by His saying: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward, and I am not of those who pretend"﴾ [Sad: 86], and other verses. This is the view of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl.

This view is not accepted, because love for the Prophet ﷺ, restraining harm from him, love for his relatives, and drawing near to Allah through obedience and righteous deeds are among the obligations of religion. These are the sayings of the early scholars regarding the meaning of the verse, so it is not permissible to resort to abrogating any of these matters.

His saying: ﴿except affection for relatives﴾ is not an exception connected to the first part, such that it would be a reward in return for conveying the message. Rather, it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes it), and its meaning is: "But I remind you of affection for relatives, and I remind you of my kinship with you," as we have related in the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam: "I remind you of Allah regarding my household."

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And whoever commits a good deed, We increase for him therein goodness﴾. That is: whoever increases in obedience, We increase for him therein goodness through multiplication. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of sins, ﴿Appreciative﴾ of the little, until He multiplies it.

[[In manuscript "B": "yaktasib" (he earns/acquires).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 42, verse 24:

﴿Or do they say﴾. Rather, they say, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿"He has invented a lie against Allah. But if Allah willed, He would seal up your heart"﴾. Mujahid said: He would bind your heart with patience so that their harm would not weigh heavily on you, and their saying that you are a fabricator. Qatadah said: It means He would seal your heart, causing you to forget the Qur'an and what came to you. He informed them that if he had invented a lie against Allah, Allah would do to him what He mentioned about him in this verse. Then He began, saying: ﴿"And Allah erases falsehood"﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: There is inversion (*taqdim wa ta'khir*) in it, its meaning being: "And Allah erases falsehood." It is in the nominative position, but the waw was omitted from it in the *Mushaf* (the written codex) according to the pronunciation, just as it was omitted from His saying: "﴿And man prays﴾" (al-Isra: 11) and "We will call the guards of Hell" (al-Alaq: 18). He informed that what they say is falsehood, which Allah will erase. ﴿"And establishes the truth by His words"﴾, that is, Islam through what He sent down of His Book. Allah has done this: He erased their falsehood and raised the word of Islam. ﴿"Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts"﴾. Ibn Abbas said: When the verse "Say, I do not ask you for it any reward except affection for relatives" was revealed, some people were troubled by it and said, "He wants to urge us to [love] his relatives after him." Then Jibril descended and informed him that they had accused him, and He revealed this verse. The people then said, "O Messenger of Allah, we testify that you are truthful." So He revealed:

﴿"And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants"﴾.

﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ [[See: al-Qurtubi: 16/26.]] Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: He means His friends and those who obey Him. It was said: repentance (tawbah, turning back to Allah) is abandoning sins, both in intention and in action, and turning toward obedience, both in intention and in action. Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: Repentance is moving from blameworthy states to praiseworthy states.

﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾, when they repent.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani told us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Yahya ibn Hammad told us: Abu 'Awanah told us, from Sulayman, from al-A'mash, from 'Umarah ibn 'Umayr, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, who said: I entered upon 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud) to visit him, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant than a man, I think he said [in a desert] [[In manuscript B: "bedawiyyah" (a desert).]] that is deadly, with his mount carrying his food and drink. He dismounted and slept, then woke up to find his mount had gone astray [[In manuscript B: "had been lost."]]. He searched for it until thirst overcame him, and he said: I will return to the place where my mount was and die there. He returned, dozed off, then woke up and found it with him, with its food and drink on it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Da'awat, Bab al-Tawbah: 11/102; and Muslim in Kitab al-Tawbah, Bab fi al-Hadd 'ala al-Tawbah wa al-Farah biha, no. (2744): 4/2103, and the wording is his; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/84-85.]]

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan told us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj told us: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah and Zuhayr ibn Harb both said: 'Umar ibn Yunus told us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar told us: Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah told us: Anas ibn Malik, who was his paternal uncle, told me, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is far more delighted at the repentance of His servant when he turns to Him than any one of you who was on his mount in a barren wilderness, when it ran off from him with his food and drink on it. He despaired of it, came to a tree, lay down in its shade, having given up on his mount. While he was in that state, behold, it was standing before him. He took hold of its reins, then said, out of extreme joy: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord,' erring out of extreme joy." [[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Tawbah, Bab fi al-Hadd 'ala al-Tawbah wa al-Farah biha, no. (2747) 4/2104, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/87-88.]]

﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾, so He erases them when they repent.

﴿And He knows what you do﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "taf'alun" with the letter ta' (addressing the listeners), and they said: it is addressed to the polytheists. The others read it with the letter ya' (third person), because it comes between two reports about a people: before it, "from His servants," and after it, "and He increases them from His bounty."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 42, verses 26–27:

﴿And He responds to those who believe﴾ [i.e., and He answers those who believe] [[Addition from manuscript "b".]], ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ when they call upon Him. ʿAṭāʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: "and He rewards those who believe."

﴿And increases them from His bounty﴾ beyond the reward of their deeds, as an act of His grace. Abu Ṣāliḥ said concerning it: "He intercedes for them on behalf of their brothers, and increases them from His bounty." He said: "On behalf of the brothers of their brothers."

﴿But the disbelievers, for them there is a severe punishment﴾.

﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants﴾. Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: "This verse was revealed concerning us. We looked at the wealth of the Banu Qurayza, the Banu al-Nadir, and the Banu Qaynuqaʿ, and we wished for it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse." [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 434.]] "And if Allah had extended provision": He expanded provision ﴿for His servants﴾, ﴿they would have rebelled﴾: they would have transgressed and become insolent, ﴿in the earth﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Their rebellion (*baghy*) is their seeking one rank after another, one mount after another, and one garment after another."

﴿But He sends down﴾ their provision ﴿in measure, as He wills﴾, as He wills, out of consideration by Him for His servants. ﴿Indeed He is Acquainted with His servants, Seeing﴾.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ṣāliḥī informed us: Abu ʿUmar Bakr ibn Muḥammad al-Muzanī informed us: Abu Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah, grandson of al-ʿAbbas ibn Ḥamzah, narrated to us: al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl al-Bajalī narrated to us: Abu Ḥafṣ ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd al-Dimashqī narrated to us: Ṣadaqah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah: Hisham al-Kinani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), from Jibril, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine has declared war against Me. I become angry for My friends as the fierce lion becomes angry. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his tongue with which he speaks, his hand with which he strikes, and his support. If he calls upon Me, I answer him; if he asks Me, I give him. I do not hesitate about anything I am going to do as I hesitate about taking the soul of My believing servant, who dislikes death, and I dislike to harm him, but he must die. Among My believing servants is one who asks Me for the door of worship, and I withhold it from him lest self-admiration enter him and corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whose faith is set right only by wealth, and if I made him poor it would corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whose faith is set right only by poverty, and if I made him rich it would corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whose faith is set right only by health, and if I afflicted him with sickness it would corrupt him. Among My believing servants is one whose faith is set right only by sickness, and if I restored him to health it would corrupt him. Indeed I manage the affairs of My servants with My knowledge of their hearts; indeed I am Knowing, Acquainted." [[Cited by al-Suyuti in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 7/353 from Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Kitab al-Awliya'*, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in *Nawadir al-Usul*, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nuʿaym in *al-Hilya*, and Ibn ʿAsakir in his *Tarikh*. See also Ibn Rajab, *Jami' al-ʿUlum wa-l-Hikam*, p. 338.]]

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain﴾, meaning the rain, ﴿after they have despaired﴾, meaning after people have given up hope of it. That is more conducive to their gratitude. Muqatil said: Allah withheld the rain from the people of Makkah for seven years until they despaired. Then Allah sent down the rain, and so Allah reminded them of His blessing. ﴿And spreads His mercy﴾ means He spreads out His rain, as He said: "And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy" [al-A'raf 7:57]. ﴿And He is the Protector﴾ of the people of His obedience, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ in the sight of His creation.

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed in them of living creatures. And He is, when He wills, competent to assemble them﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is for what your hands have earned﴾. The people of Madinah and Syria read "bi-ma kasabat" without the fa' (the conjunction "fa", "so/then"), and it is written so in their copies of the Qur'an (maṣāḥif, sing. muṣḥaf). Whoever omits the fa' makes the "ma" at the beginning of the verse mean "that which", so the meaning is: "that which has afflicted you is because of what your hands have earned."

﴿And He pardons much﴾. Al-Hasan said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, there is no scratch of a twig, nor stumbling of a foot, nor twitching of a vein, except because of a sin, and what Allah pardons is greater." [[Narrated by Hannad as a mursal report (a report whose chain omits a companion) in al-Zuhd: 1/519. It has supporting reports in al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, and in al-Tabarani from the hadith of al-Bara'. See the commentary on the Kitab al-Zuhd in the same place. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/354 to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

He said: "I will explain it to you, O Ali: whatever sickness, punishment, or trial you suffer in this world is for what your hands have earned. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is too generous to punish them twice in the Hereafter, and what Allah has pardoned you in this world, Allah is too forbearing to return to after His pardon." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 1/85, and al-Hakim: 4/388. Al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/354 added its attribution to Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Mani', Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh. Then Allah mentioned retaliation, saying: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [He called the recompense an evil], though it is not an evil in itself, because the two resemble each other in form. Muqatil said: It means retaliation (qisas) for wounds and bloodshed.

Mujahid and al-Suddi said: It is the answer to the ugly person who says, "May Allah disgrace you," so you say, "May Allah disgrace you," and if he insults you, then insult him with the like of it, without transgressing.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: I said to Sufyan al-Thawri, "What is the meaning of His words, mighty and majestic, 'And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it'?" He said: "That a man insults you and you insult him, and that he does to you and you do to him." I did not find anything with him, so I asked Hisham ibn Hujayra about this verse, and he said: "The one who wounds is retaliated against; it is not that he insults you and you insult him."

Then Allah mentioned pardon, saying: ﴿But whoever pardons﴾ the one who wronged him, ﴿and makes reconciliation﴾ by pardon between himself and his wrongdoer, ﴿his reward is with Allah.﴾ Al-Hasan said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: "Whoever has a reward with Allah, let him stand up." None will stand except those who pardoned, and then he recited this verse. ﹟[Reported by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/359.]﹠ ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: those who begin with wrongdoing.

﴿And whoever retaliates after being wronged﴾ i.e., after the wrongdoer has wronged him, ﴿those﴾ meaning the ones who retaliate, ﴿there is no blame upon them﴾ with punishment or censure.

﴿The blame is only upon those who wrong the people﴾ who begin with wrongdoing, ﴿and oppress within the earth without right﴾ they act in it with acts of disobedience. ﴿For them is a painful punishment.﴾

Nafi' read "أَوْ يُرْسِلُ" with the lam in the nominative (raf'), on the basis of inception (ibtida', beginning a new clause), and "فَيُوحِي" with the yaa unvocalized (sakinah). The others read it with the lam and the yaa in the accusative (nasb), by coordination (ataf) with the grammatical position (mahall) of "الْوَحْي" (revelation), because its meaning is: "It is not for a human that God should speak to him except that He reveal to him, or send a messenger."

﴿Indeed He is Most High, All-Wise﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 42, verses 52–53:**

﴿And thus﴾, that is, just as We revealed to the rest of Our messengers, ﴿We revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾. Ibn Abbas said: prophethood. Al-Hasan said: mercy. Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: revelation. Al-Kalbi said: the Book. Al-Rabi' said: Jibril. Malik ibn Dinar said: it means the Qur'an.

﴿You did not know﴾ before the revelation, ﴿what the Book was, nor faith﴾, meaning the laws (shara'i') and the markers (ma'alim) of faith. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma said: [[See: Sahih Ibn Khuzayma: 2/160.]] "Faith" in this place means prayer, and its evidence is the words of the Mighty and Majestic: "And Allah would never let your faith go to waste" (al-Baqarah 143).

The people of Usul (the scholars of the foundations of religion) hold that the prophets, upon them be peace, were believers before the revelation. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to worship Allah before the revelation according to the religion of Ibrahim, but the laws of his religion had not been made clear to him.

﴿But We made it a light﴾. Ibn Abbas said: meaning faith. Al-Suddi said: meaning the Qur'an. ﴿By it We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾, that is, We give direction by it. ﴿And indeed, you guide﴾, that is, you call, ﴿to a straight path﴾, meaning Islam.

﴿The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned﴾, that is, the affairs of all creation in the Hereafter.
